blocks.text: Two glasses on a rock overlooking a mountain lake near El Chaltén, Argentina
El Chaltén, Argentina: glasses by the lake with snowy peaks behind them
El Chaltén: Laguna de los Tres

Today’s full-day hike takes us towards Mount Fitz Roy and Laguna de los Tres.

A minibus picks up participants from their hotels in the morning. The trail starts near Hostería El Pilar, about 18 km from El Chaltén.

The route begins in lenga and ñire forests along the Río Blanco. After climbing for about 1 hour and 15 minutes, you reach a viewpoint overlooking the Piedras Blancas Glacier.

About 45 minutes farther along, the trail reaches Poincenot Camp, where hikers from around the world often pitch their tents. The route then crosses the river on a suspension bridge and reaches Río Blanco base camp, which climbers use. The national park has a shelter here in case of bad weather.

For participants who feel up to a more strenuous hike, the guide offers the option of climbing to Laguna de los Tres. This section gains about 500 m of elevation and takes roughly an hour. From the top, you can see the Fitz Roy massif, the lake and the glaciers. Laguna Sucia is also visible nearby. The final climb is considerably steeper than the earlier sections and is the most demanding part of the day.

After a rest and lunch, we descend to El Chaltén, passing the Laguna Capri viewpoint on the way back.
Mountain lake below snowy slopes and a sharp peak near El Chaltén, Argentina
